doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Country Preacher, dynamics, and the Velvet Note video
summary: Rowe brings up Cannonball's Country Preacher album and Jesse Jackson; Parsons says dynamics and arc matter, and they discuss a video from the Velvet Note club.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: That’s really precious. You know it occurred to me this morning, I saw Jesse Jackson had passed away, and so I had to go get this out. I don't know if you can see that or not.
Yeah. I see what that is, yeah.
And “Country Preacher,” that was Jesse Jackson.

And that album has just fascinated me, the recording when they did “Country Preacher” that place, that church was packed with people and they just went crazy. It was a real lesson in dynamics and so forth.

Yes. Yeah dynamics are so important. When we hear straight ahead jazz a lot of times we hear, you play the song form, you know and it’s you know like this, everybody shows all the licks that they know and it’s like this. But to me music – you go on a journey.
I saw a video, I think it was a club called The Velvet Note?
Oh in Atlanta, well outside of Atlanta.

Yeah. And I wrote down one comment on it – two actually. And one was dynamics because your pieces were very, as you said, like it had an arc to it and some high points and very, very interesting. I think it was called, one of them was called “Forest Song” is that correct?
Were you playing a bass recorder or something?
